name: enhancer of zeste 2 polycomb repressive complex 2 subunit

function.text: EZH2 encodes the catalytic methyltransferase component of polycomb repressive complex 2, which methylates histone H3 lysine 27 to regulate transcriptional repression.

function.text: EZH2 encodes the catalytic methyltransferase component of polycomb repressive complex 2, which methylates histone H3 lysine 27 to regulate transcriptional repression. Based in part on similarity, it is a catalytic subunit of the PRC2/EED-EZH2 complex, a Polycomb group (PcG) complex that methylates 'Lys-9' (H3K9me) and 'Lys-27' (H3K27me) of histone H3, leading to transcriptional repression of the affected target gene. It displays a preference for substrates with less methylation, loses activity when progressively more methyl groups are incorporated into H3K27, H3K27me0 > H3K27me1 > H3K27me2. Compared to EZH1-containing complexes, it is more abundant in embryonic stem cells and plays a major role in forming H3K27me3, which is required for embryonic stem cell identity and proper differentiation.

germline.text: Pathogenic germline variants are associated with Weaver syndrome (autosomal dominant).

somatic.text: Somatic alterations involving EZH2 have been reported in follicular lymphoma, primary myelofibrosis, and acute myeloid leukemia.
